## Excursions to Ahu Akivi on Easter Island: four itinerary options

[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) is one of the most recognizable archaeological monuments on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/). Seven moai stand on its platform, restored in the 20th century. Unlike many coastal complexes, this platform lies inland. The stone figures face towards the ocean, while local oral tradition links them to seven voyagers sent to Rapa Nui on the orders of Hotu Matu'a.

We include Ahu Akivi on several current standalone excursions. When comparing them, look beyond photographs of the seven statues to the other stops, duration and stated format. Some combine Akivi with the red-stone quarry; others add the Tahai ceremonial complex or the unrestored platform at Hanga Poukura.

## Excursions that include Ahu Akivi

Our selection includes [“Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau”](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/), lasting about 4 hours. It introduces the restored platform and the source of the red stone used to make the statues' topknots.

[“Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai”](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai/) adds a third monument. The terms explicitly specify a private format. The catalog also offers [“Easter Island: Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai”](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai-visit/), but a similar sequence of stops does not mean identical services; check the terms of each published program.

Finally, [“Ahu Akivi, Hanga Poukura, Puna Pau and Tahai”](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) is a separate 4-hour private excursion with an English-speaking guide. It includes an unrestored platform, allowing you to compare two states of archaeological preservation in one day. A Russian-speaking guide is listed as an optional extra at an additional cost.

| Itinerary | What is added |
|---|---|
| Akivi + Puna Pau | Red-tuff quarry |
| Akivi + Puna Pau + Tahai | Coastal ceremonial complex |
| Akivi + Hanga Poukura + other stops | Unrestored platform |

## Why combine Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau?

At [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), red volcanic stone was quarried for *pukao*, the topknots visible on some moai. This adds important context to Ahu Akivi: creating monumental sculpture required quarrying materials, shaping individual pieces and moving heavy stone elements.

At Ahu Akivi itself, observe the line of figures and the position of the monument in the surrounding landscape. Restoration in 1960 was an important archaeological conservation project on Rapa Nui. Legends and scientific interpretations of the statues' purpose sometimes emphasize different ideas; oral traditions are best understood as living heritage, not a definitively proven account of events.

Choosing a route via [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) adds several restored platforms, including Ko Te Riku, whose statue has reconstructed eyes. A visit to [Hanga Poukura](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/) lets you see moai still lying on the ground and discuss the fate of ancient ahu after their original period of use.

## What to consider before traveling

These excursions have similar names but different confirmed conditions. One lasts around 4 hours, another specifies a private format, while the four-stop itinerary separately states guide language and the availability of an additional service. Do not automatically apply these features to every itinerary.

Rapa Nui's archaeological sites are part of a protected national park. Check current official rules for access, approved viewing routes, guide requirements and ticket validity for your dates. The moai and stone platforms are not free-standing objects to climb or touch.

Sun and wind protection and suitable footwear for uneven ground are useful on the island's open sites. Allow time for photographs and your guide's explanations rather than rushing each platform to fit in more stops.

## Frequently asked questions about Ahu Akivi excursions

### Do all Ahu Akivi tours visit Tahai?

No. The [“Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau” route](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) has a different, shorter list of stops. Tahai appears in several extended versions.

### Where can I see unrestored moai in this area?

The published [four-stop excursion](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) includes [Ahu Hanga Poukura](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/), where fallen statues and parts of the platform remain.

### How long does an Ahu Akivi excursion last?

The catalog includes options lasting around 4 hours or exactly 4 hours. For a program without a stated duration, confirm it for that itinerary rather than guessing from a similar title.

### Can I request a Russian-speaking guide?

On the [route via Hanga Poukura](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/), this is an optional paid service. Check the separate terms for other programs.

## Excursions to Ahu Hanga Poukura: seeing a monument before restoration

At [Ahu Hanga Poukura](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/) on Easter Island, an ancient stone platform survives alongside fallen moai. The most striking feature is its archaeological condition: sculptures lie on the ground and the structure appears as surviving fragments. This kind of monument tells the history of Rapa Nui as powerfully as the famous rows of upright statues.

We include Hanga Poukura on excursions through central [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), alongside restored [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/), the [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) quarry and coastal [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/). Together, the stops reveal different aspects of Rapa Nui heritage in one outing.

## What a visit to Hanga Poukura reveals

* Ahu* are ceremonial stone platforms of communal and spiritual significance in Rapa Nui culture. Moai are associated with the memory of ancestors. Not all island statues survived upright; historical changes and later restoration of selected complexes have become part of the preservation story.

At Hanga Poukura, visitors can observe large stone blocks, the position of sculptural fragments and the surrounding landscape. A guide's explanations are especially valuable: without them, it is difficult to distinguish original construction from later changes or understand what remains in place. Fallen moai should not be seen as a poorly arranged exhibition; their condition is an authentic part of the island's archaeological history.

Rapa Nui National Park has been on UNESCO's World Heritage List since 1995. Its significance encompasses not only large restored ensembles but also many archaeological sites documenting the development of island society.

## Current excursions that include Hanga Poukura

[“Ahu Akivi, Hanga Poukura, Puna Pau and Tahai”](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) is a 4-hour private excursion. Its terms specify an English-speaking guide, with Russian-language guiding available as an optional paid extra. It visits a restored platform, an unrestored structure, the red-tuff quarry and Tahai in sequence.

Another option is [“Easter Island: Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai”](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai-visit/). Its description also mentions unrestored Hanga Poukura en route to those named monuments, and its linked catalog includes the site. However, the private format and four-hour duration of the first option should not automatically be attributed to the second; check its terms separately.

| What to compare | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Stops | Hanga Poukura is not on every Akivi itinerary |
| Duration | 4 hours is specified for a particular program |
| Guiding | Language and supplements depend on the excursion |

## Restored and fallen moai: why see both?

[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) is known for its even row of seven raised moai, which helps visitors imagine a ceremonial platform as a complete structure. At Hanga Poukura, the monument's long history remains visible in fallen statues, structural fragments and weathered stone.

Continuing to [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) adds the material context: red stone was quarried here for the *pukao* topknots of some moai. [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) displays another architectural arrangement near the coast. These stops explain the making, placement and modern preservation of monuments far better than several isolated photographs of similar figures.

## Preparing for a visit

Coastal archaeological sites are exposed to wind and may have uneven surfaces. Closed-toe shoes and clothes suitable for changing weather are more practical than beachwear alone. Access requirements and guide obligations follow the current national park rules, which should be checked before traveling.

Stay on approved visitor paths. Do not approach sculptures simply to touch them or get a dramatic photograph: archaeological details are vulnerable even when the stones appear massive. Designated viewing points provide ample photographic opportunities.

Departure times, the order of stops and the guide's language must be confirmed for the selected route. This is particularly important for two geographically similar programs with different levels of published commercial detail.

## Frequently asked questions about Hanga Poukura excursions

### Why are Hanga Poukura's moai lying down?

Hanga Poukura is presented as an unrestored ceremonial site. The statues' positions reflect the monument's historical condition; the same excursion can compare it with a restored platform.

### Is there a private excursion that visits the site?

Yes. The [Ahu Akivi, Hanga Poukura, Puna Pau and Tahai route](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) is listed as a 4-hour private tour.

### Must I visit other platforms together with Hanga Poukura?

The published Ada Tours offerings include Hanga Poukura on multi-stop routes. A standalone excursion devoted exclusively to this platform is not listed in the catalog considered here.

### Can I book a Russian-speaking guide?

The four-stop private itinerary offers that option at an additional charge. Confirm availability and terms when planning.

## Excursions to Ahu Nau Nau: moai beside Anakena Beach

[Ahu Nau Nau](/chile/place/ahu-nau-nau/) stands beside [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/). Its ceremonial platform, with restored moai, is close to pale sand and palm trees. The contrast between ancient stone figures and the beach landscape makes this a memorable stop.

We include Ahu Nau Nau on full-day excursions along Rapa Nui's southern coastline. They begin at other archaeological sites, pass through the famous quarry and large platforms, and then reach Anakena. It is therefore a full sightseeing day, not just a short walk on the beach.

## What is Ahu Nau Nau?

The moai on this platform retain distinctive carved details. Archaeological work at Ahu Nau Nau has been particularly important for understanding how the statues were finished: elements of moai eyes were found during excavations. The Rapa Nui Museum records restoration of the complex in 1978.

Ahu Nau Nau is part of the cultural landscape of UNESCO-listed Rapa Nui National Park. Archaeological-area rules apply. The beach and protected archaeological site may have different access conditions, even though they are next to each other.

At Anakena, it is best to distinguish two activities: first concentrate on the monument and its history, then spend time beside the sea if your chosen itinerary provides for it and the weather permits.

## Which Ada Tours excursions visit Ahu Nau Nau?

[“Easter Island South Coast and Anakena Beach”](/chile/easter-island/south-coast-moai-anakena-private/) is a full-day private excursion with an English-speaking guide. Its route includes [Ahu Vaihu](/chile/place/ahu-vaihu/), [Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/), [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/), Ahu Nau Nau and Anakena. This particular program includes a packed lunch, with a Russian-speaking guide available at an additional charge.

[“Easter Island: South Coast and Private Picnic at Anakena”](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-south-coast-anakena-private-picnic/) also visits the principal archaeological monuments and ends at Anakena. It includes a private picnic overlooking the coast. The first itinerary has different terms: they are two separate products.

| Option | Distinctive feature |
|---|---|
| South Coast and Anakena | Private excursion, packed lunch |
| South Coast with picnic | Private picnic at Anakena |

## Why visit Anakena after Rano Raraku and Tongariki?

[Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is the quarry where much of the island's moai were carved. Statues in different stages of construction and movement remain on its slopes. [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is known for fifteen restored moai on a large platform. After those stops, Ahu Nau Nau offers a different setting: statues immediately beside a sandy shore.

The combination helps explain the journey from quarrying stone to erecting figures and preserving monuments. Each stop on the excursion answers a different question. There are many sites, so a worthwhile visit requires sensible time allocation rather than an equally lengthy stop at every monument.

## Preparing: archaeology, sunshine and beach time

Rapa Nui's open sites can be windy; closed-toe shoes, sunscreen and water are useful for inspecting stone structures and walking along paths. Bring separate clothing if you may swim. Entering the ocean depends on waves, weather and local instructions, so swimming cannot be guaranteed on every day.

Before traveling, check national park visitor rules, admission and guiding requirements, and the length of free time at Anakena. The word “beach” in an excursion title does not mean you will spend most of the day by the sea. If beach relaxation is the priority, choose accordingly.

## Frequently asked questions about Ahu Nau Nau excursions

### Does a visit to Ahu Nau Nau include Anakena Beach?

Yes. Both named excursions visit [Ahu Nau Nau](/chile/place/ahu-nau-nau/) and [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) in the final stage of the route.

### Do all excursions to Anakena include a picnic?

No. A private picnic is explicitly part of the [“South Coast and Private Picnic” itinerary](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-south-coast-anakena-private-picnic/). The other option specifies a packed lunch.

### Can I visit only Ahu Nau Nau without a full day of excursions?

It is a separate archaeological monument near the beach, but Ada Tours' current catalog offers it on multi-stop itineraries. Do not assume a short standalone excursion is automatically available.

### Which other moai sites appear on the south-coast trips?

Current itineraries list [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), Ahu Te Pito Kura and other sites. Check the exact stops on each itinerary page.

## Excursions to Ahu Te Pito Kura on Easter Island

[Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/) is an archaeological stop on Rapa Nui containing one of the largest moai ever transported from the Rano Raraku quarry. It is known as Paro. Unlike the restored upright statues at [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), this moai lies beside its ancient ceremonial platform. Its position is important to understanding island history: visitors see a monument in a condition associated with the period when the statues fell.

Ada Tours visits Te Pito Kura as part of an extended itinerary along the island's eastern and southern coasts. A short excursion dedicated solely to this site should not be confused with the published full-day programs.

## What you see at this stop

The main monument is Paro, a long stone figure lying beside the platform. According to Rapa Nui National Park, it stood about 10 meters tall; a large red stone *pukao* topknot is nearby. The site makes clear how challenging it was to transport and erect statues carved from volcanic tuff.

Near the archaeological zone is a place often called the “Navel of the World” in tourist accounts and associated with traditional beliefs about the site's power. Local legends provide valuable cultural context, but stories about the stone's “energy” should not be presented as scientifically proven physical effects.

## Ada Tours routes via Te Pito Kura

We offer several excursions visiting this location:

- [“Anakena, Rano Raraku and Ahu Tongariki”](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/): a full day featuring the quarry, moai platforms, Te Pito Kura and a finish at Anakena Beach. A packed lunch is listed.
- [“Easter Island South Coast and Anakena Beach”](/chile/easter-island/south-coast-moai-anakena-private/): a full-day private tour with an English-speaking guide and packed lunch. Te Pito Kura follows Rano Raraku and Tongariki.
- [“South Coast and Private Picnic at Anakena”](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-south-coast-anakena-private-picnic/): an itinerary with the same principal archaeological stops but a special focus on a picnic beside the ocean.

The main choice is therefore **the day's format and how the itinerary finishes**, rather than three different ways of seeing the fallen moai. “Private” in the third title alone does not establish a particular vehicle class or hotel standard.

## Combining Te Pito Kura with other places

Before this stop, visitors typically discover Rano Raraku, the ancient quarry where moai were carved, and [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) with 15 raised statues. Afterwards, the route may continue to [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) and [Ahu Nau Nau](/chile/place/ahu-nau-nau/). This combination provides an unusual chance to see, in sequence, how statues were made, a restored platform and a fallen giant.

| Stop | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Rano Raraku | Moai quarry |
| Tongariki | 15 upright statues |
| Te Pito Kura | Fallen Paro |
| Anakena | Beach and ahu |

For a stay of several days on the island, compare the [three-day Ada Tours itinerary](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/): Te Pito Kura features on the south-coast day, with other days devoted to Orongo, Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau.

## Visitor rules and preparation

Ahu Te Pito Kura is part of the national park's archaeological heritage. Park-management rules require an admission ticket and an accredited guide. Our **three-day tour** includes the park ticket; for each **standalone excursion**, check whether it is included in that particular offer rather than assuming the multi-day tour's inclusions apply.

Approaching monuments too closely, touching them or crossing protective barriers is forbidden where posted. Comfortable shoes and wind and sun protection are useful even for short stops: the coast is exposed to the weather.

## Frequently asked questions about Te Pito Kura

### Can I see upright moai here?

The main moai, Paro, lies on the ground. Itineraries visit [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) to see a row of restored upright statues.

### Can Te Pito Kura and Anakena be visited on the same day?

Yes. All three Ada Tours excursions listed combine this monument with other archaeological stops and Anakena Beach.

### Is national park admission included in every excursion?

No such blanket inclusion is stated. The ticket is explicitly included in the [three-day tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/); check the terms of each standalone excursion.

## Excursions to Ahu Tongariki: 15 moai of Easter Island

[Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is Rapa Nui's largest restored ceremonial platform. **15 moai** stand on it, facing inland, with the Pacific coastline beyond their silhouettes. It is one of the principal archaeological stops on a journey to Easter Island: here you can see an entire monumental ensemble rather than one individual statue.

Context matters when choosing an excursion. A visit to Tongariki is especially rewarding after the Rano Raraku quarry, where the stone figures were carved, and before seeing monuments preserved in a different condition. The processes of making, erecting, toppling and restoring moai then become understandable through real sites.

## What makes Tongariki special?

Fifteen statues form a long row on an extensive stone platform. Their proportions, heights and facial features differ. The site has been restored, so its present appearance is the result of archaeological conservation, while the complex itself belongs to Rapa Nui heritage. The national park is UNESCO World Heritage-listed.

Do not expect permission to approach the statues closely. Designated viewpoints provide the full effect, revealing the row and the moai's scale against the coastal landscape. Sunrise photography is famous here, but **a sunrise departure is not specified** in the confirmed terms of the full-day Ada Tours excursions below.

## Ada Tours excursions that include Ahu Tongariki

- [“Anakena, Rano Raraku and Ahu Tongariki”](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/) is a full-day tour stopping at Akahanga, the quarry, Tongariki, Te Pito Kura and Anakena Beach. A packed lunch is mentioned.
- [“Easter Island South Coast and Anakena Beach”](/chile/easter-island/south-coast-moai-anakena-private/) is a full-day private excursion with an English-speaking guide and packed lunch. It also visits [Ahu Vaihu](/chile/place/ahu-vaihu/), where fallen moai lie beside an old platform.
- [“South Coast and Private Picnic at Anakena”](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-south-coast-anakena-private-picnic/) is a cultural route through the main monuments with dedicated time for a picnic by the ocean.

All three go to Tongariki. If archaeology is your primary interest, compare the number of stops and time for the guide's explanations. To combine monuments with a longer beach stay, pay attention to how the day ends at Anakena and the exact meal arrangements.

## How Tongariki differs from nearby ahu

| Site | What you will see |
|---|---|
| Tongariki | 15 standing moai |
| [Ahu Vaihu](/chile/place/ahu-vaihu/) | Fallen statues |
| [Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/) | Giant moai Paro |
| Rano Raraku | Statues near the quarry |

These monuments tell different parts of one story. If you want to understand how moai were made and used, it would be a pity to reduce the visit to a single photo stop at Tongariki. On the other hand, a full coastal sightseeing day may be more practical than several separate transfers on a short trip.

[“Easter Island: Three Days among Moai and Volcanoes”](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) includes Tongariki on day two, with separate excursions to Orongo and western monuments on other days. It suits visitors seeking more than just the best-known statues.

## Planning and access to the national park

Rapa Nui is far from mainland Chile, and archaeological sites are scattered across the island. Coastal weather matters even under a sunny forecast: exposed areas can be windy. Bring sun protection, water and footwear suitable for uneven paths.

Official national park regulations require an admission ticket and accredited guide. Admission is included in the [three-day tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/); check each standalone excursion's inclusions. Archaeological sites cannot be treated as freely accessible places without an entry permit.

## Frequently asked questions about Ahu Tongariki

### How many moai stand on the platform?

The restored platform at Ahu Tongariki holds **15 moai**.

### Can I combine Tongariki with the Rano Raraku quarry?

Yes. All three listed full-day Ada Tours excursions include that combination.

### Do these excursions include sunrise at Tongariki?

A separate sunrise outing is not specified in the published listings. It must be arranged separately and should not be assumed to be part of the usual daytime itinerary.
